subject: Order Form indemnity: evidence ownership, escrow trigger, and IP claim flow
messages:
From: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@novacorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: maya.patel@novacorp.com; sales@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form — indemnity & evidence ownership questions

Dylan / Redwood team,

Thanks for the updated order form. A couple narrow points from our legal/procurement side we need to lock before we can proceed to signature:

1) Evidence ownership and custody: if Novacorp is required to produce materials as part of responding to a third-party IP claim (logs, model prompts, debug traces), we need clarity on who retains copies and how long Redwood will keep our submissions. We have internal rules about retention and data exports — we cannot hand over long-term copies without explicit custody/return provisions.

2) Escrow / remediation trigger: there is concern about when an escrow or repair fund becomes payable. Novacorp would prefer a clear threshold (e.g., final adverse judgment or written settlement) rather than a mere claim notice.

3) Defense control carveout: we understand you want to retain defense control; we need an assurance Novacorp can step in if Redwood unreasonably refuses to defend.

I'm attaching a redline plus an evidence-ownership matrix that spells out what types of artifacts Novacorp expects to keep copies of vs. what we expect Redwood to retain. Can your legal team advise on workable language for custody, retention, and escrow triggers?

We'd like to get this closed this week. Happy to hop on a short call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Sanjay Iyer
Head of Legal Operations, Novacorp

Attachments: Novacorp_redlines_20270228.pdf, evidence_ownership_matrix.csv

From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@novacorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — indemnity & evidence ownership questions

Sanjay — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Jordan (account lead).

Quick read: we are broadly aligned on limiting long-term custody of Novacorp artefacts on our side; the ask is mostly about ensuring we have the necessary evidence to investigate and, if needed, defend. Practical asks from our side: short-term retention (30–90 days) for debugging/forensics + a defined export procedure.

On escrow triggers, I hear you on preferring final judgment or settlement. From our pricing and risk side, we normally allow earlier remediation funding on a candidate determination (a claim that is substantiated by prima facie evidence) but are flexible on thresholds for this customer given enterprise concerns.

Kimberly / Marissa — can you propose redline language that: (a) allows Redwood to request and retain a short export of evidence for defense and triage (specify file types, max retention), (b) defines escrow/remediation trigger options (settlement/judgment vs. prima facie), and (c) adds a step-in / reasonableness carveout for the defense control item?

Jordan — Novacorp wants this closed rapidly; any commercial levers (cap, escrow size, SOW options) worth proposing so legal can pick an acceptable path?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: recommended_redlines_kpark_20270228.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: dylan.brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — indemnity & evidence ownership questions

Team — read Novacorp's redline. High-level positions below (I attached a tracked-redline doc).

1) Evidence custody/retention: propose a compromise — Redwood will accept production of evidence artifacts (logs, prompts, model IDs, limited transcripts) and may retain a single forensic copy for up to 60 days solely for the purposes of investigating and defending the claim. After 60 days Redwood will either: (i) securely delete the copy unless continued retention is agreed in writing; or (ii) return the artifacts to Novacorp. Add a confidentiality carve: Redwood will not use customer artifacts to train models or for product analytics.

2) Escrow / remediation trigger: offer two-tier approach in order form: (a) default trigger = final adverse judgment or written settlement; (b) optional accelerated remediation (for an increased escrow amount or capped remediation reserve) triggered on a good-faith substantiated finding (prima facie) with independent expert validation. This gives Novacorp the certainty they want while allowing commercial flexibility.

3) Defense control: keep Redwood's primary defense control but add a limited right for Novacorp to assume control if Redwood declines to defend within a defined time period or acts unreasonably. Also include standard cooperation/step-in mechanics and allocation of reasonable defense costs.

4) Cap and insurance: propose offering a modest cap arrangement (e.g., $5M) combined with requirement that Redwood maintain commercial liability insurance; for large customers we can surface alternate higher caps for negotiation.

I'll attach the proposed language. If Novacorp insists on unlimited retention or automatic escrow on notice, that's a non-starter.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: recommended_redlines_kpark_20270228.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@novacorp.com>, dylan.brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: kimberly.park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — indemnity & evidence ownership questions

Sanjay — appreciate the fast turnaround. Two commercial proposals to help bridge to signature: 

Option A (default): Redwood accepts Kimberly's compromise (60-day forensic retention; delete/return thereafter), defense control with Novacorp step-in right, and default escrow trigger = final judgment/settlement. Cap = $5M.

Option B (accelerated): If Novacorp requires an earlier remediation trigger (prima facie), Novacorp would pre-fund an escrow equal to 6 months of committed spend (capped at $1M) and accept a smaller cap of $3M. Escrow is released on settlement/judgment or converted to remediation fund following the validated prima facie finding.

We believe Option B addresses Novacorp's desire to act faster while protecting Redwood commercially. Which option would you prefer? Happy to discuss on a quick call tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Accounts — West, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@novacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, dylan.brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: maya.patel@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-03-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — indemnity & evidence ownership questions

Jordan / Dylan — thanks all for the options and Kimberly's language. Novacorp legal prefers Option B (accelerated) but will need confirmation on two points before we can queue signature:

1) The independent expert validation process for a prima facie finding — we need a short description of how that expert would be selected and what standard of proof they use.

2) Escrow mechanics — can Redwood accept a neutral escrow agent (we propose IronBank Escrow Services) and describe how funds are released on conversion to remediation.

If you can confirm these two items, we'll finalize procurement approvals; otherwise we'll take Option A under protest. Can we do a 20-minute call tomorrow morning PST to finalize?

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Legal Operations, Novacorp

---
Thread note: attachments referenced above include Novacorp_redlines_20270228.pdf (customer redlines with highlighted custody/escrow asks), evidence_ownership_matrix.csv (artifacts list), and recommended_redlines_kpark_20270228.docx (Redwood legal's proposed language).
